A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same V-PET study. All 23 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support reliable comparison despite relocation and reformatting.

before.justification: V3 reports original classification experiments, ensemble analyses and hyperparameter-selection results in Table 3 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results, including Table 3, the tuning comparison now in Section 6.3, and detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: The V-PET procedure is unchanged: supervised PEFT, one-hot pseudo-label generation, averaging across models, and single-round self-training. Algorithm 1 changes only in formatting.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six VTAB datasets and retain the CIFAR-10/100 and Food-101 probing comparisons. V4 explicitly groups the six datasets into Natural, Specialized and Structured categories without changing coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets are unchanged, including FixMatch, FlexMatch, SoftMatch, FineSSL, labeled-only training and ST. The individual-validator and random-selection baselines also remain in the relocated tuning comparison.

E3.justification: The reported splits, shot counts, model configurations, training settings, evaluation metrics and hyperparameter search spaces are retained. Moving the tuning analysis into Section 6.3 introduces no new protocol.

E4.justification: The ensemble-size and strategy analyses, weaker-model ensemble experiment, initialization study and classifier-head comparisons are unchanged. V3 Appendix B.7 becomes v4 Section 6.3 with the same tuning analysis; the added runtime discussion provides no new experimental ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five runs for the ensemble-scaling analysis. Mean and standard deviation reporting for tuning errors already appears in v3 Table 11 and is retained in v4 Table 4.

E6.justification: V4 Section 5.2 newly states that estimated V-PET runtime is about 1.16 times that of other SSL baselines, without a detailed timing protocol. Matched accuracy values, ranking and scaling plots, and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, pseudo-label equations and validator definitions remain unchanged. Appendix C corrects 'Rank Index' to 'Rand Index' without changing the ARI formula or mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction and shortened conclusion retain the same contributions: evaluating SSL with VFMs, establishing labeled-only PEFT as a strong baseline, and exploiting complementary pseudo-labels through ensembling.

C2.justification: V4 adds an explanation that self-training dominates runtime while the other ensemble stages incur limited overhead. Appendix D extends the existing classification-scope statement by explaining that detection and segmentation may require task-specific architectures and training, limiting direct applicability.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 adds relative runtime information and identifies the stages contributing to computational cost. Hardware disclosures, implementation settings, hyperparameter ranges and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds Sun et al., 'A stronger mixture of low-rank experts for fine-tuning foundation models,' as reference 60 in the introductory PEFT discussion. The broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 clarifies the dataset-category explanation, corrects terminology, shortens the conclusion and updates author and conference information. It moves Appendix B.7 into Section 6.3 and adds Appendix D, while retaining the overall narrative.

P2.justification: Main tables gain colored dataset labels and cleaner percentage formatting, and Table 3 is enlarged and relocated. The tuning table moves from Appendix Table 11 to main-text Table 4; the scaling figure is relocated and Figures 5–6 are renumbered. Their plotted content is retained.

improvement.justification: V4 modestly improves readability and qualification: the main results table is clearer, existing tuning validation is easier to find in Section 6.3, and Appendix D explains limits on transfer beyond classification. The experimental evidence remains unchanged, and the new runtime estimate lacks a detailed timing protocol.
